tools.name: list_services
tools.description: List all monitored services with their current status (OK, DEGRADED, DOWN, PAUSED, PENDING). Call this first to get an overview of infrastructure health, or to find a service's ID.

tools.name: get_service
tools.description: Get one service's details including its 10 most recent health checks (status codes, latency, errors). Call this when diagnosing WHY a service is degraded or down.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: List incidents — open ones by default, or recently resolved with status='resolved'. Call this when asked about outages, what's broken, or incident history.

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: Get an incident's full record: timeline of every update, escalations, runbook results, AI summary, and post-mortem if drafted. Call this before acting on an incident.

tools.name: acknowledge_incident
tools.description: Acknowledge an open incident, stopping further escalation. Call this when the user says they are looking into an incident or asks you to take ownership of it.

tools.name: resolve_incident
tools.description: Mark an incident as resolved, with an optional note describing the fix. Only call this when the user confirms the underlying issue is fixed — resolving is a status-page-visible action.

tools.name: who_is_on_call
tools.description: Get the person currently on call for each on-call schedule, and when their shift ends. Call this when deciding who to contact about an incident.

tools.name: list_anomalies
tools.description: List recent learned-baseline latency anomalies: observed vs baseline response time, the deviation z-score, how many consecutive hours it has been sustained, and the incident it auto-opened (if any). Call this when asked why a service is slow, about latency spikes, or for early degradation signals th

tools.name: diagnose_incident
tools.description: Analyze an open incident and recommend the next action: run a specific runbook, escalate to a human, resolve, or wait. Returns the recommendation (with rationale and confidence) and the candidate runbooks. This is analysis ONLY — it does not change anything. Call this to decide what to do about an i

tools.name: run_runbook
tools.description: Execute one specific runbook against an incident. This MUTATES INFRASTRUCTURE (it can restart or scale services). Only call after diagnose_incident recommended it AND the user has confirmed. Pass the runbookId from the diagnosis's recommendation or candidate list.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "diagnose_incident" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_incident · Private data: get_incident, who_is_on_call · Public sink: get_incident · Destructive: diagnose_incident, run_runbook.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_incident · Private data: get_incident, who_is_on_call · Public sink: get_incident · Destructive: diagnose_incident, run_runbook

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
